title: Representation Learning on Hyper-Relational and Numeric Knowledge Graphs with Transformers

problem.claim: Hyper-relational knowledge graphs may contain numeric information in triplets or qualifiers, but existing embedding methods assume entities are discrete objects.

gap.claim: Existing hyper-relational knowledge graph embedding methods do not represent numeric values within triplets or qualifiers.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes HyNT, a unified framework for learning representations of hyper-relational knowledge graphs containing numeric literals in triplets or qualifiers.
HyNT uses context and prediction transformers that model triplet-qualifier correlations together with numeric information.
HyNT learns compact triplet and qualifier representations to reduce transformer computation cost.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that HyNT can predict missing numeric values as well as missing entities or relations in a hyper-relational knowledge graph.
The authors report that HyNT achieves significantly better results than state-of-the-art methods on real-world datasets.

narrative_sequence.summary: Hyper-relational knowledge graphs associate triplets with qualifier relation-entity pairs.
Numeric information can occur in triplets and qualifiers, but existing methods assume discrete entities.
HyNT provides a unified representation-learning framework with context and prediction transformers that incorporate correlations and numeric information.
Compact triplet and qualifier representations reduce transformer computation cost.
HyNT supports missing-value prediction and is reported to outperform state-of-the-art methods on real-world datasets.

source_observation.claim: A unified representation-learning framework can incorporate numeric literals alongside entities, relations, and qualifiers.

interpretation.claim: Handling heterogeneous value types within one graph representation may broaden the prediction tasks supported by the model.

application.claim: For knowledge graphs containing measurements or dates, consider modeling numeric values directly rather than forcing them into discrete entities.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach transfers beyond the reported real-world datasets or which numeric types are supported.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, metrics, or numerical effect sizes.
The abstract does not provide implementation details or ablation results.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or reproducibility.
